You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 17, has left education or training and been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to start by understanding your situation.

**First, let me ask about your child (or children):**

Do you have a child or children you're responsible for? If yes, could you tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine the right path through the eligibility assessment. Child Benefit eligibility depends significantly on the age of the child, with different rules applying if they are:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 or over

What are the ages of the child or children you'd like to claim for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is between 16-19 years old, there are additional requirements to check. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now, for a 16-19 year old like Alex, eligibility depends on their education or training status.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (attending school, college, or approved training courses), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR
3. **Neither** of the above (not in education/training and didn't recently leave)

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has left school, but he recently signed up with the local careers service to figure out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me clarify Alex's situation a bit more:

**When did Alex leave education?** Was it:
- Within the last 20 weeks (about 5 months), or
- More than 20 weeks ago?

Also, to be clear:
- Is Alex currently enrolled in any approved education or training program (like college, sixth form, or an approved training course)?
- Or has he completely left education and is now just receiving careers guidance?

The distinction is important because:
- If he's **currently in approved education/training**, different rules apply
- If he **recently left education** (within 20 weeks) and is registered with careers services or similar, he may be eligible for an extension period
- If it's been more than 20 weeks since he left education and he's not currently enrolled in anything, different rules would apply

Could you help me understand the timeline and whether he's enrolled in any current education or training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's completely left education - he's not enrolled in any college or training program right now. He left school a couple of months ago and then registered with the careers service to get some help figuring out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying! So Alex left education a couple of months ago (which is within the 20-week window) and has registered with the careers service. This means he may be eligible for an extension period.

Let me navigate to check the extension eligibility rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 17 years old (so he's 16-17 age range)
- He left education a couple of months ago (within the 20-week window)
- He has registered with the local careers service (which is a qualifying service)

This means Alex **is eligible for the 20-week extension period**! This extension is specifically designed for young people in Alex's situation.

**Important to know:** The extension will end either:
- At the 20-week mark after he left education, OR
- When Alex turns 18, whichever comes sooner

Now let me check the next requirement - there's one more question:

**Is Alex working full-time?** (Full-time generally means 24 hours or more per week)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
So the next question is:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Children aged 16 or over who work 24 or more hours per week are not eligible for Child Benefit (unless they're also in approved education or training, which Alex isn't currently).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now. He's just been focusing on meeting with the careers service to work out his options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is not working at all, which means he meets this requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in his own name

If Alex is NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right, that's fine and we can continue. If he IS receiving these benefits, that would affect eligibility.

Does Alex receive any benefits in his own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship program?**

If he is, I'll need to know which type, as different apprenticeships have different rules:
- All apprenticeships in England would disqualify him
- Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland would disqualify him
- In Wales, Foundation Apprenticeships are approved, but other apprenticeships would disqualify him

Is Alex in any apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just registered with the careers service trying to figure out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so he meets this requirement too. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status. This is about where **you** (the claimant) live and your immigration status.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, there are some special circumstances that might still qualify you, such as:
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Having pre-settled status with certain conditions (working, studying, or having sufficient resources)
- Being a Crown servant living abroad

What is your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This can be satisfied in any of these ways:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be - or the equivalent in kind - towards their care, such as food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which clearly establishes your responsibility for him. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

If someone else is claiming, it's important to know because:
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at the same time
- If both parties agree you should be the claimant instead, that can be arranged
- If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to make the decision

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital** (as an inpatient)?
2. **In local authority care** (such as a children's home or residential care)?
3. **Being fostered** by someone else?
4. **Living normally** with you at home?

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

For example, is the council providing any financial support for Alex's living costs or housing?

If the council is NOT paying for Alex (which would be the normal situation for a child living at home with their parent), then we can proceed to the final outcome.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension** - He's 17, left education a couple of months ago (within the 20-week window), and has registered with the careers service, which is a qualifying service

✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - He's not in paid work at all

✅ **Alex doesn't receive benefits** - He's not claiming ESA, Universal Credit, or similar benefits in his own right

✅ **Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - Alex is not currently in any apprenticeship program

✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK (Manchester)

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives at home with you

✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

✅ **Normal living situation** - Alex lives at home and the council isn't paying for his accommodation or maintenance

### Important Reminder About the Extension:

The 20-week extension period will end either:
- **20 weeks after Alex left education**, OR
- **When Alex turns 18**, whichever comes sooner

After this period, if Alex hasn't started approved education, training, or an approved apprenticeship, the Child Benefit would stop.

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000
5. **Payments are made every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can start your claim here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the claiming process?
